clue.text: Peanuts, or a little bread?

definitions.meaning: informally, peanuts is a trivial sum of money
petty means little and bread is slang for money, so a small fund kept for minor office spending

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses point to a small float of money kept on hand for minor expenses, which is trivial in amount.

clue.text: Fertiliser? Ditch the lot, they said!

indicators.note: the setter signals that the words before are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a fosse is a ditch or moat, and one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A gardener told to throw away the whole bag of fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: FOSSE (a defensive ditch) followed by FATE (lot), spoken together, sound like the chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Salts of phosphoric acid are a principal ingredient of many fertilisers; the question mark shows the definition is by example.

clue.text: Old character, a source of irritation in the flesh

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Old English and Icelandic runic alphabet, written like a p with a tall stem

definitions.text: a source of irritation in the flesh
definitions.meaning: the idiom for a persistent nuisance, from a sharp prickle lodged under the skin

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an obsolete runic letter for the th sound; the other the prickle of a rose, as in the biblical phrase for a constant irritant.

clue.text: The old round-the-island line for small farmers

parts.note: ye is the old way of writing the definite article
a round shape looks like the letter O
the Isle of Man, the island in the Irish Sea
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An old railway line running around an island, serving the local smallholders.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were farmers owning modest freeholds, and the collective term covers that class of smallholders.

clue.text: Not qualified to play rival

definitions.meaning: without any limitation or reservation, total
Captain Jack ... is a leading character in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals, so an actor playing a rival takes this part

explanation.surface: Someone lacking the credentials to compete against an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconditional and unrestricted are synonyms for the first sense; the second is the surname of Sheridan's hero in The Rivals.

clue.text: Large lump round a hip

indicators.note: the lump goes round, enclosing the single letter

parts.note: a hunch is a thick piece or chunk

explanation.surface: A doctor noticing a big swelling around someone's hip.
explanation.definitionFit: The hindquarter of a person or animal, including the hip and buttock, is the synonym here.

clue.text: Some indication of Sanskrit, etc

indicators.note: only part of the following word is taken, the letters running at its start

explanation.surface: A clue to what Sanskrit and related tongues are like.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indic branch of the Indo-European family includes Sanskrit, Hindi and Bengali, hence the etc.

clue.text: To make a clean cut is nice work

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Praise for a surgeon's neat incision.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut into something sharply and precisely, as an engraver or surgeon does, is the verb sense.

clue.text: The Good Food Guide?

parts.note: the name of a famous restaurant handbook is reread as a person who guides people towards healthy eating

explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition expert advises clients on wholesome diet, so is literally a guide to good food.

clue.text: An easy task the soldier at the top finds hard

parts.note: C-in-C, the commander-in-chief, is the highest-ranking soldier
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Even the general in charge finds this simple job difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is a certainty or a very easy undertaking, an informal synonym.

clue.text: What comparisons were to Dogberry

parts.note: Dogberry, the bungling constable in Much Ado About Nothing, garbles the saying that comparisons are odious, swapping in a word meaning smelly

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's malapropism replaces the word for hateful with one meaning having a strong scent.

clue.text: Spotted the relative article

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone saw the piece about a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as a past tense, seen, but it means stained or dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted in the sense of soiled or blemished is a synonym for impure or dirty.

clue.text: The sort of car for a go-between, say

indicators.note: the word before is to be pronounced, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a pander is a go-between in illicit love affairs, a pimp

explanation.surface: A question about which car suits an intermediary.
explanation.walkthrough: A PANDA car is the British name for a small police patrol car, once painted in black and white panels.
explanation.definitionFit: British police patrol cars were nicknamed after the black-and-white bear because of their two-tone livery.

clue.text: Skilled artisan who is amusing to love

definitions.text: Skilled artisan who is amusing to love

parts.words: Skilled artisan who is amusing to love
parts.note: alludes to the proverb that love laughs at locks and the craftsmen who make them, since lovers always find a way

explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes and mends locks is the one the old saying says love mocks.

clue.text: Like Hook, capital of Holland for example

parts.note: as means like, in the way of
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A comparison of Captain Hook with the first city of the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter of Holland is H, a breathed sound, which is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H stands for a breathy consonant sound, which phoneticians call by this name.

clue.text: Church music for a simple hymn

parts.note: plain means simple or unadorned
a hymn is a song of praise

explanation.surface: Choosing church music for an uncomplicated hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied liturgical chant such as Gregorian chant is the type of ecclesiastical music meant.

clue.text: Champ has light meal

definitions.meaning: to champ is to chew or munch noisily
a snack, as in grabbing something to eat

explanation.surface: A champion who eats a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to munch with the teeth, the other a quick snack.

clue.text: Rose perhaps is after the fruit drink

indicators.note: the rosé comes after the fruit in the finished word

parts.note: the elder is the tree whose berries are the fruit
rosé is an example of wine

explanation.surface: A girl named Rose wants some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as a name or a flower, but stands for the pink wine rosé.
explanation.definitionFit: A homemade beverage fermented from elderberries is the alcoholic drink meant.

clue.text: The work sounds inconsistent, like Faust for example

parts.note: OP is the abbreviation for opus, a work

indicators.note: the following word is heard rather than spelt, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: erratic means inconsistent or irregular

explanation.surface: A critic finding Goethe's Faust uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: Gounod's Faust is an opera, which makes 'like Faust' a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gounod's setting of the Faust story is a grand opera, so it has that quality.

clue.text: Lid for the mouth ointment

parts.note: a balm is a soothing ointment
oral means relating to the mouth

explanation.surface: A cap for a jar of lip salve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' is slang for a hat; a Balmoral is a flat Scottish bonnet, named after the royal castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lid is slang for a hat, and this is a Scottish bonnet named after the royal estate.

clue.text: By God, an early Degas perhaps!

indicators.note: signals that the remaining letters may be arranged another way
an early version is cut short, so the name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation on discovering an early painting by Degas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' cuts the last letter from DEGAS, leaving DEGA, and 'perhaps' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic mild oath, a softened form of a vow by the deity.

clue.text: The odds came down and caused dislocation

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
rain comes down, so rained means came down

explanation.surface: Betting odds dropped and upset everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench a joint by twisting its ligaments injures it much as putting it out of place does.

clue.text: Supine sort of judge

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, so the letters are sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A description of a lazy kind of judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A puisne judge is a junior judge of the English High Court.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior High Court judge in England is known by this title, from Old French for younger.

clue.text: Confuses and dismisses batsman

definitions.meaning: in cricket a wicketkeeper puts out a batsman who is out of his ground by breaking the wicket

explanation.surface: A bowler who baffles and gets the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to baffle; the other is the cricket dismissal where the keeper breaks the wicket.

clue.text: It transfers power to a director

definitions.meaning: a material or wire that carries electricity or heat
one who directs an orchestra or choir

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a body that carries electric current; the other a person leading an orchestra.

clue.text: Firm support for a king perhaps

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A company backing a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king' is a monarch on the surface, but the king cobra is a species of the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is one species of the hooded venomous snake, a definition by example.

clue.text: One who is very near to a French sea-girt island

indicators.note: girt means surrounded, so the sea encircles the island

parts.note: mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: Someone living close to an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is an old word for tight-fisted, so a very near person is a hoarder of money.

clue.text: One of three divinities in India — five in a Muslim sect

definitions.text: One of three divinities in India

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the sect's name

parts.note: the Shia are one of the two main branches of Islam
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A Hindu deity found among Muslim believers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hindu trinity is Brahma, Vishnu and this god, the destroyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinduism's trimurti comprises Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and the destroyer god.

clue.text: May Molly embrace the saints!

indicators.note: Molly's surname goes round the two letters for saints

parts.note: Molly Bloom is the heroine of James Joyce's Ulysses
S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for plural

explanation.surface: A blessing wishing that Molly hug the saints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' reads as a wish, but it is hawthorn flowers, called may in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the hawthorn's flower, so the definition names a particular flowering.

clue.text: Sentence ends in one of these stops

parts.note: a term is a prison sentence
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remark about where sentences finish, at full stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' suggests punctuation, but means the end stations of railway or bus lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stations on transport routes are the end stops of the line.

clue.text: Maintain the fit is about right

indicators.note: the fit goes round the letter for right

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering

explanation.surface: Insisting the clothes suit almost correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a position is to contend or assert it in debate.

clue.text: Ill at ease with this official absenteeism? Certainly!

definitions.text: Ill at ease with this official absenteeism? Certainly!

parts.words: Ill at ease with this official absenteeism? Certainly!
parts.note: a person who is unwell can be at ease, off work with permission, while unwell and excused duty

explanation.definitionFit: Authorised time off work granted because of illness is the officially sanctioned absence.
